scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The work provides a well-defined and rigorously evaluated approach to set-based reranking for iterative agentic search. The experiments include competitive baselines, clear ablations demonstrating the utility of both SFT and RL stages, and robust external corroboration via objective exact-match RAG evaluations.

Set-level rubrics.Set-level rubrics evaluate the
overall quality of a document set. We consider
three dimensions: (1)Relevance, which measures
whether the document set covers the key informa-
tion needs and diverse answer aspects required
by the query; (2)Conciseness, which measures
whether the set contains little repetitive, redundant,
or irrelevant content; and (3)Consistency, which
measures whether key facts, claims, and conclu-
sions across documents are mutually compatible
rather than contradictory.

et al., 2017),

evidence.excerpt:
We evaluate RubricRanker on both deep research
and RAG benchmarks and report the results in Ta-
bles 1 and 2, respectively. We make the following
observations:
(1) RubricRanker demonstrates superior per-
formance in both deep research and RAG sce-
narios.On deep research benchmarks, Rubr-
icRanker achieves the best average score of
60.1, outperforming the second-best baseline,
Rank4Gen, by 2.6 points. On RAG benchmarks,
RubricRanker also obtains the highest average EM
score of 40.0, surpassing Rank4Gen by about 2
points. These consistent improvements demon-
strate that rubric-based reranker training can select
document sets that better support downstream LLM
generation.
(2) Generation-oriented rerankers do not
generalize to deep research tasks.Generation-
oriented rerankers clearly improve over vanilla
rerankers on RAG benchmarks, where Rank4Gen
outperforms BGE-Reranker-Large by 1.8

Despite the effectiveness of RubricRanker, our
work still has several limitations. (1) The con-
struction of rubric-based rewards relies on GPT-5.1,
which can be costly when scaling to large training
corpora. In the future, we plan to train a special-
ized reward model to provide more cost-effective
and efficient rubric-based feedback. (2) Due to the
high cost of LLM calls and the slow test-time infer-
ence of deep research agents, we sample a subset
of queries for evaluation on deep research bench-
marks. In future work, we will consider evaluating
on the full benchmark sets to provide more compre-
hensive results. (3) Our evaluation still depends on
the final generation quality of LLM agents. Even
when RubricRanker selects a high-quality docu-

reasoning or generation. Developing more objec-
tive metrics to directly evaluate the

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Exact-match accuracy on five established RAG benchmarks provides an objective, evaluator-independent measurement that corroborates the headline gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream generation quality measured by LLM judges on deep research benchmarks and exact-match string scoring on five RAG benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GPT-5.1-generated query-specific rubrics used for SFT teacher labels and GRPO reward scoring during training.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains of 2.6 points average on deep research benchmarks and about 2 points EM on RAG benchmarks over strong baselines (such as Rank4Gen and SetR) directly support the claims of improved set selection and cross-task generalization.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The model is evaluated across four deep research benchmarks (HealthBench, WebWalkerQA, DRB, ResearchQA) using standard agent evaluation frameworks and five RAG benchmarks evaluated on exact match (EM), supported by comprehensive ablations and search-call efficiency analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective exact match (EM) accuracy on five established RAG benchmarks (HotpotQA, Bamboogle, NQ, PopQA, TriviaQA) where RubricRanker consistently outperformed all vanilla and generation-oriented baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream generation quality assessed by LLM judges on official deep research protocols (GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash) and exact match (EM) string scoring on five standard RAG benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GPT-5.1 generated query-specific rubrics used for SFT teacher labels and GRPO reward evaluation during training.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss dependency on costly proprietary LLMs for rubric scoring during training, the evaluation of sampled query subsets for deep research, and confounding downstream agent generation errors.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing query collection across deep research and RAG scenarios, rubric synthesis using GPT-5.1, teacher SFT annotation, and GRPO reward aggregation combining set and document scores.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a well-defined and rigorously evaluated approach to set-based reranking for iterative agentic search. The experiments include competitive baselines, clear ablations demonstrating the utility of both SFT and RL stages, and robust external corroboration via objective exact-match RAG evaluations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RubricRanker, a document set reranker optimized via hierarchical search rubrics covering set-level (relevance, conciseness, consistency) and document-level (authority, timeliness) properties using rubrics-guided SFT and GRPO reinforcement learning.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a well-defined and rigorously evaluated approach to set-based reranking for iterative agentic search. The experiments include competitive baselines, clear ablations demonstrating the utility of both SFT and RL stages, and robust external corroboration via objective exact-match RAG evaluations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss dependency on costly proprietary LLMs for rubric scoring during training, the evaluation of sampled query subsets for deep research, and confounding downstream agent generation errors.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
